previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of coronary artery bypass grafting, mitral valve replacement, congestive heart failure, atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease, and peripheral vascular disease with a nonhealing left heel ulcer was admitted for worsening lower extremity edema and suspected urinary tract infection. She had been recently discharged after a left lower extremity angiogram and reported increasing swelling despite home diuretics. She was treated with IV furosemide followed by oral torsemide, achieving a negative fluid balance and improvement in edema and renal function. Hyperkalemia on admission was managed with insulin and dextrose. A presumed UTI was treated with three days of IV ceftriaxone, but urine culture showed no growth, so antibiotics were discontinued. ABI/PVR testing confirmed severe bilateral aortoiliac occlusive disease. The patient declined inpatient rehabilitation and opted for home discharge with home health services. She was discharged on doubled torsemide dose, with close cardiology follow-up and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.
